messages.subject: function to plot from columns
parts:
Hi everyone

I have a dataframe like this:

d<-replicate(10,rnorm(5))
dimnames(d)<-list(c(),paste("c",1:10,sep="."))
d<-as.data.frame(d)

i want to be able to build up a plot from columns of d, like this if i do it manually:

ggplot(aes(x=c.1,y=c.2,color="pair1"),data=d)+geom_line() +geom_line(aes(x=c.3,y=c.4,color="pair2")) +geom_line(aes(x=c.5,y=c.6,color="pair3")) +geom_line(aes(x=c.7,y=c.8,color="pair4")) +geom_line(aes(x=c.9,y=c.10,color="pair5"))

however i want to be able to get this from a function, so actually i want to be able to get this same plot by writing some kind of function

myfplot(d$c.1,d$c.2,"pair1")+myfplot(d$c.3,d$c.4,"pair2")+etc

but i can't figure out how to write myfplot.  ive tried

myfplot<-function(x,y,label) { ggplot(aes(x=x, y=y, color=label))+geom_line() }

but it says "doesn't know how to deal with uneval", not least because there's no "data" in the ggplot. 

i also think im creating the colors wrong, sometimes it complains that "pair1" is not a color and expects something like "blue", and id like to give the axes labels other than the default.

Any help would be greatly appreciated!
-Neal

Hi Neal,

Could this be what you want instead?

d<-replicate(10,rnorm(5))
dimnames(d)<-list(c(),paste("c",1:10,sep="."))
d<-as.data.frame(d)

d$row<-1:5
d.melt<-melt(d,id.vars="row")
ggplot(d.melt,aes(variable,value,group=row))+geom_line()

messages.subject: Re: function to plot from columns
parts:
Hi:

This problem is a lot easier once you know how to organize your data. If I understand this correctly, the odd numbered columns are meant to represent x's, the even numbered columns y's and you want a factor to distinguish each pair of columns. Normally I would use the reshape package, but I don't know know how to melt two separate sets of columns, so I'll use the reshape() function from base R instead.

drs <- reshape(d, varying = (list(c('c.1', 'c.3', 'c.5', 'c.7', 'c.9'),
     c('c.2', 'c.4', 'c.6', 'c.8', 'c.10'))), v.names = c('x', 'y'),
     times = paste('Pair', 1:5, sep = ''), direction = 'long')
dim(drs)
# [1] 25  4
names(drs)[1] <- 'Pair'
head(drs)
          Pair          x          y id
1.Pair1 Pair1  0.3164601  0.3735933  1
2.Pair1 Pair1 -0.2137418  0.3387708  2
3.Pair1 Pair1  0.4653958 -2.7626807  3
4.Pair1 Pair1  1.0986535  1.6515445  4
5.Pair1 Pair1  0.4263354  2.6489088  5
1.Pair2 Pair2 -1.0502965 -0.2973519  1

If the row names annoy you, you can always write row.names(drs) <- NULL. Once the data are properly shaped, it's pretty straightforward:

ggplot(drs, aes(x, y, color = Pair)) + geom_line(size = 1)

HTH,
Dennis

messages.subject: Re: function to plot from columns
parts:
Neal, I think it's easier if you melt the data before plotting. And then do some changes in your data to fit ggplot.

d <- melt(d)
d$num <- as.numeric(gsub("c.", "", as.character(d$variable)))
d$odd <- as.logical(d$num %% 2)

d_reshaped <- cbind(d[d$odd, c("variable", "value")] , d[!d$odd, c("variable", "value")])
names(d_reshaped) <- c("x_name", "x", "y_name", "y")
d_reshaped$x_name <- d_reshaped$x_name[,drop = TRUE]


ggplot(data = d_reshaped, aes(x, y, colour = x_name)) + geom_line() +
  scale_colour_hue("Pair", breaks = levels(d_reshaped$x_name),
  labels = paste("Pair", 1:5))

You could make a function of these code.
Hope that helps
Luciano
